gaps.sentence: It is Saturday tomorrow, so I ___ get up early.
gaps.hint: an absence of obligation at weekends
gaps.explanation: 'Don't have to' shows there is no obligation: don't have to get up.

gaps.sentence: Although the road was blocked, we ___ reach the hospital in time.
gaps.explanation: For a single past achievement, 'was/were able to' is used, not 'could'.

gaps.sentence: We ___ have hurried — the concert was cancelled anyway.
gaps.hint: the rush turned out to be unnecessary
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't have hurried' means we hurried although it was unnecessary: needn't have.

gaps.sentence: I ___ see the sea from my bedroom window when I was little.
gaps.explanation: Verbs of perception use 'could' for past ability: could see.

gaps.sentence: You have been travelling all day, so you ___ be exhausted.
gaps.hint: an obvious conclusion from known facts
gaps.explanation: A logical conclusion from known facts uses 'must': must be exhausted.

gaps.sentence: If I were you, I ___ take the earlier train.
gaps.hint: if I were you plus would
gaps.explanation: 'If I were you' is followed by 'would': would take.

gaps.sentence: You ___ be starving — you haven't eaten since breakfast.
gaps.explanation: 'Must' expresses a logical deduction about the present.

gaps.sentence: The lights are on, so they ___ be home.
gaps.explanation: 'Must' expresses a confident conclusion from evidence.
